body:
### The problem

The TypeScript tokenizer keeps a name and the `?` after it together, so that
the optional marker of `name?: T` is not a ternary. The rule takes every
`name?` that is not followed by `?` or `.`, including the condition of a
ternary written without spaces:

```js
function pick(x, y) {
  return x?y:0;
}
```

```
$ lizard a.js          # master, 01afe9c
       3      1     13      2       3 pick@1-3@a.js
```

Here `x?` is one token and the cyclomatic complexity of `pick` is 1 instead of
2 in .js and .ts. The TSX tokenizer has the opposite problem: it has no such
rule, so the optional markers of a class field and of the parameters count as
ternaries in .tsx and .jsx:

```tsx
class A {
  name?: string;
  m(a?: number, b?: string) { return 1; }
}
```

```
$ lizard a.tsx         # master, 01afe9c
       1      3     16      2       1 m@3-3@a.tsx
```

### What changes

`lizard_languages/tsx.py` and `lizard_languages/typescript.py`. A `?` now
stays with its name only when a `:`, `,`, `)` or the end of the source follows
it, which is where an optional marker can stand and a ternary cannot; .ts,
.js, .tsx and .jsx share the rule. With the fix:

```
       3      2     14      2       3 pick@1-3@a.js
       1      1     14      2       1 m@3-3@a.tsx
```

### How it is tested

Tests in `test/test_languages/testOptionalOperators.py`, 3 of which fail on
`master` without the change. The full suite passes on the branch:
`python -m pytest test` gives 1671 passed, 7 skipped. pycodestyle reports no
new warnings in the changed files.

### What does not change

Optional chaining `?.` and nullish coalescing `??`, which keep their own
tokens.

Thanks for maintaining lizard and for taking the time to look at this.

commits.messageBody:
The TypeScript tokenizer keeps a name and the "?" after it together, so
that the optional marker of "name?: T" is not a ternary. The rule takes
every "name?" that is not followed by "?" or ".", including the condition
of a ternary written without spaces:

    function pick(x, y) {
      return x?y:0;
    }

Here "x?" is one token and the cyclomatic complexity of pick is 1 instead
of 2 in .js and .ts. The TSX tokenizer has the opposite problem: it has
no such rule, so the optional markers of a class field and of the
parameters, "name?: string" and "m(a?: number, b?: string)", count as two
ternaries in .tsx and .jsx.

A "?" now stays with its name only when a ":", ",", ")" or the end of the
source follows it, which is where an optional marker can stand and a
ternary cannot; .ts, .js, .tsx and .jsx share the rule.
commits.messageHeadline: Count a JavaScript/TypeScript ternary written without spaces

title: Count a JavaScript/TypeScript ternary written without spaces
